title: Independent stitch image observation report v1
description: Strict emitted observation record, bounded to 16 MiB at publication. All eight ordered definition/result pairs preserve the existing stitch-metric v1 constraints. The CLI produces observations through Parse, Evaluate and Serialize. The serializer validates field shapes, supported outcome/presence, hash syntax and exact decimal bounds; it does not remeasure a hand-built Evaluation. JSON Schema cannot express observation joins or recompute measurements. Explicit external-mask coverage is an observation domain, not proof of faithful geometric validity, physical quality, or product acceptance.

metricDefinition.title: A0 stitch metric definition v1
metricDefinition.description: Reproducible measurement semantics only. Product acceptance values are deliberately outside this contract. Successful result rounding uses a binary64 representation-safety contract: decimalPlaces is 0 through 9, and the result schemas require the exact scaled magnitude |rawValue * 10^decimalPlaces| to be at most 2^39. This is a numeric representability boundary, not a product-quality limit; JSON Schema states the per-decimal-place raw/value ranges and runtime validation rechecks the scaled value.

rounding.description: Rounding is defined only inside the exact-safe binary64 range documented above. The result schemas apply the decimalPlaces-specific rawValue/value ranges; runtime validation additionally checks the exact decimal scaled value.

metricResult.title: A0 stitch metric result v1
metricResult.description: One result bound at runtime to an exact metric definition. It carries both raw and rounded values but no product acceptance value. Successful rawValue and value use an exact-safe binary64 rounding contract: |rawValue * 10^decimalPlaces| must be finite and at most 2^39. The conditional ranges below are the schema-side raw/value projection of that scaled rule; runtime validation performs the strict scaled check. Nonnegative integer counters are bounded by 2^53-1 for exact binary64 interoperability. These are representability boundaries, not product-quality limits.
